prop:q-game-of-life:
Proposition The quantum Game of Life (q-GoL) as a Toffoli-defined aether automaton. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q and Planck time t_P(q) = 1/\hbar_q. Let \mathcal{L} \subset M be a discrete sublattice of brane points \{p_i\}. Each site carries a qubit |\psi_i\rangle \in \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. The q-Game of Life (q-GoL) is the discrete-time invertible cellular automaton

  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
    \colon  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}}
    \to  \mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{L}},
  \qquad
  |\Psi(t{+}1)\rangle
   = 
  \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}}
  |\Psi(t)\rangle.

The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is constructed entirely from q-deformed Toffoli gates acting on Reeb bundle fibres of neighbour sites. The construction requires five properties:

  1. Building block. The transition operator is the q-AND gate:
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \colon  |c_1, c_2, t\rangle
  \longmapsto
  |c_1, c_2,  t \oplus_q (c_1 \wedge_q c_2)\rangle.

The symbol \wedge_q denotes the Hecke-algebra q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q), given under Well-definedness condition below. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q executes in three Planck steps.

No control-independent factor \Phi(q) lies in the image of the three-strand Toffoli construction (Toffoli transfer matrix); \wedge_q is evaluated directly via P_{7,6}(q).

  1. Superposition. Cell states admit superpositions |\psi_i\rangle = \alpha_i|0\rangle + \beta_i|1\rangle via Hadamard rotations H \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{S}_{p_i}). The set \{\mathrm{Toff}_q, H\} is universal for reversible computation, in the sense of Bennett, for every q > 0: reversible universality needs the gate to be invertible with a firing target-flip channel, both of which item 4 and the non-vanishing of P_{7,6} on q \neq 1 supply.

Scope of universality. The standard Toffoli-plus-Hadamard quantum universality theorem applies to unitary gates, whereas \mathrm{Toff}_q is provably not unitary for q \neq 1. Whether a non-unitary invertible gate set can be universal in a quantum sense is unsettled, so item 2 states reversible universality only.

  1. Conway's rules as Toffoli circuits. Survival (k = 2, 3) and birth (k = 3) at site i with neighbourhood N(i) are enacted by the composite operator
  \mathcal{U}_i^{\mathrm{rule}}
   = 
  \prod_{\{j_1, j_2\} \subset N(i)}
  \mathrm{Toff}_q
  \!\left(
    |\psi_{j_1}\rangle,  |\psi_{j_2}\rangle;  |\psi_i\rangle
  \right).

Ancilla qubits encode the neighbour sum. A ripple-carry adder of O(|N(i)|) Toffoli gates computes the binary count k.

  1. Reversibility. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q is invertible, with
  \sigma_i^{-1}
   = 
  \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot \mathbb{1},

so \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is invertible and the automaton is reversible. It is not unitary away from the classical limit: the eigenvalues of \sigma_i are q and -q^{-1}, of modulus \neq 1 for q \neq 1, so no inner product makes \mathrm{Toff}_q unitary, and the Markov trace form has a nontrivial radical at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Reversibility in the sense a reversible cellular automaton requires — invertibility of the tick — therefore holds for every q > 0, being a property of the quadratic relation alone and independent of the amplitude signs discussed below; unitarity holds only at q = 1.

  1. Information bandwidth budget. One generation advances in 3 |\mathcal{L}| Planck steps. The aether bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) = q \eta_q / (q - 1)^2 bounds the generation rate:
  \text{gens / sec}
   \leq 
  \frac{\mathfrak{B}(q)}{3  |\mathcal{L}|}
   = 
  \frac{q \eta_q}{3  (q - 1)^2  |\mathcal{L}|}.

Well-definedness condition. The evolution is well-defined only when the Toffoli diagonal P_{7,7}(q) is positive and the q-AND amplitude P_{7,6}(q) is non-zero. With Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the two amplitudes are

  P_{7,7}(q) \,=\, \frac{q^{3}\bigl(q^{4}+1\bigr)}{\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}},
  \qquad
  P_{7,6}(q) \,=\, -\,\frac{(q-1)(q+1)\bigl(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1\bigr)}{2q\bigl(q^{2}+1\bigr)^{2}}.

For q > 0 the first is strictly positive, having no positive root. The second vanishes exactly at q = 1: the factor (q+1) is positive there, and the sextic q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1 has no positive real root, so the whole zero set on q > 0 is carried by (q-1). The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the aether value q_0 \approx 1.110.

Non-vanishing, not positivity. The criterion is that the q-AND does not degenerate, not that it carry a particular sign. This is the same condition the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND uses — it turns on P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0 — and it is what invertibility of the tick requires. At q = 1 the q-AND vanishes and the braiding ceases to act: that is the classical limit, where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli, and it is the one point the condition excludes.

Strict positivity would be a different and stronger requirement: at z = q^3/(q^2+1) it holds only on 0 < q < 1, since P_{7,6}(q_0) \approx -0.1438, and would place the aether outside the well-defined regime. It is not the criterion in force here.

Direct LP feasibility vs. amplitude sign. Constructing the q-Toffoli as an element of H_3(q) — T_q = \sigma_1 + \hbar_\times\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 for the all-proton ordering — and evaluating the LP condition G\vec t(q_0) \geq 0 directly against the H_3(q) Markov–Gram matrix gives strictly positive components for all eight strand-type orderings (Toffoli LP-stability). Thus the aether satisfies LP feasibility as well as non-vanishing. Two structural properties qualify this: first, the Gram matrix is entrywise non-negative and \vec t is entrywise non-negative for the all-proton ordering, so positivity is forced by shape for 2 of the 8 orderings and nontrivial for the remaining 6; second, \vec t turns negative on 0 < q < 1, the opposite side of q = 1 from where P_{7,6}(q) < 0, so the amplitude sign and the LP cone condition select opposite regimes.
prf:q-game-of-life:
Proof Proof of q game of life. The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is built from q-Toffoli generators. By Toffoli transfer matrix, these act as elements of H_3(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes H_3(q) on the tensor product of Reeb bundles \bigotimes_i \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. Each generator is invertible in H_n(q), and it is invertibility — not unitarity — that this argument establishes. For real q > 0 with q \neq 1, the eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i have modulus \neq 1, so \sigma_i is not unitary with respect to any positive-definite inner product (by contrast, Squier's invariant bar-Hermitian form over \mathbb{Z}[s, s^{-1}] with s^2 = t is indefinite away from the unit circle [squier1984, Theorem, p. 199; \S 3, eq. (6), p. 201]); and the Markov trace form is not available as a Hilbert inner product on H_n(q), having a nontrivial radical at z = q^3/(q^2+1) for n \ge 3. Reversibility therefore rests on invertibility alone: the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 gives the explicit inverse

  \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot 1 ,

so every \sigma_i is a unit and the composite is invertible. The generators are not involutions at generic q: \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i holds precisely when q = q^{-1}, i.e. in the classical limit q \to 1, which is where the q-Toffoli reduces to the ordinary Toffoli gate.

Any reversible computation is simulated by Toffoli gates [bennett1973, toffoli1980, fredkin1982]. That Toffoli together with Hadamard is universal for quantum computation is the theorem of Shi and of Aharonov [shi2002, aharonov2003], stated for the standard Toffoli gate; its extension to \mathrm{Toff}_q at q \neq 1 is not established here.

The bandwidth bound follows by counting. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q in the 3-strand Hecke algebra requires three elementary crossings, taking three Planck steps. One generation applies one Toffoli gate per neighbour triple. This yields the stated bound.

The well-definedness condition requires P_{7,7}(q) > 0 and P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the diagonal is P_{7,7}(q) = q^{3}(q^{4}+1)/(q^{2}+1)^{2}; numerator and denominator are strictly positive for every q > 0, so the first clause holds throughout and places no constraint. The q-AND is P_{7,6}(q) = -(q-1)(q+1)(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1)/\bigl(2q(q^{2}+1)^{2}\bigr); for q > 0 the factor (q+1) is positive and the sextic has no positive real root, so the zero set is exactly \{q = 1\} and the second clause holds on q \neq 1. The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the aether. \square

Note that the criterion used here is non-vanishing, not positivity: invertibility of the tick and the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND require only P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. Strict positivity would restrict to 0 < q < 1 and exclude the aether.
rem:q-game-of-life-interpretation:
Remark Deterministic cellular-automaton models of Peña et al. and 't Hooft. Peña et al. construct a reversible quantum Game of Life using Toffoli-based adder circuits. Their Toffoli gate is the classical limit q \to 1 of the q-Toffoli, and their construction is recovered in that limit; away from it the two are not comparable, since the q-deformed generator is invertible but not unitary. Their unitary tick maps to 3 Planck steps. One identifies the q-deformed amplitude P_{7,6}(q) as the physical AND amplitude. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) it has a single zero on q > 0, at q = 1, and the diagonal P_{7,7}(q) has none. The well-definedness condition — the diagonal positive and the q-AND non-vanishing — therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the aether; the one excluded point is the classical limit itself, where the q-deformation contributes nothing.

The relation to 't Hooft's proposal — that quantum mechanics emerges from a deterministic Planck-scale cellular automaton — is more limited, and the limitation is structural rather than a matter of detail. The mechanism 't Hooft relies on is that a deterministic evolution permutes a distinguished basis of ontological states, so that the operator it induces on the span of that basis is automatically unitary and generates a Schrödinger flow. That step requires unitarity of the tick, and by the statement's item 4 the q-Toffoli is unitary only at q = 1.

Consequently the identification holds at q = 1 and is not established away from it. At q = 1 the tick is a permutation of basis states, the ontological states may be read as Reeb bundle fibres \mathcal{S}_p and the tick as the Planck step t_P(q) — but q = 1 is also where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli gate, so what the classical limit realizes is the construction of Peña et al. rather than anything the q-deformation contributes. At q \neq 1 the tick remains invertible, and the automaton remains deterministic and reversible in the sense a cellular automaton requires, but the induced operator is not unitary and 't Hooft's embedding does not apply as stated. Whether a deterministic automaton with an invertible non-unitary tick can support the emergence 't Hooft argues for is not addressed here.

The reading of the Markov trace as a categorical coarse-graining replacing 't Hooft's information loss is likewise not established. It is a suggestion the degeneracy of the trace form makes worth examining — a degenerate form has a radical, and quotienting by a radical is a loss of information rather than an ad hoc postulate of one — but no such identification is derived in this paper.
rem:aether-computation:
Remark Aether-independence of computation. Discrete time at the Planck scale replaces analysis with combinatorics. The Toffoli braid P_{7,6}(q) forms a rational function of the aether parameter q, carrying the numerator factor (q - 1).

This imposes three structural facts:

  1. The q-AND amplitude is non-zero for all q \neq 1.
  2. The combinatorial skeleton of reversible computation persists at every aether scale.
  3. As the universe cools from the Big Bang (q \to \infty) to the local epoch (q = q_0), the amplitude decreases but never vanishes.

The medium of computation does not alter its logic. The combinatorics depends only on the aether parameter. The Hecke crossing coefficients at q = q_0 satisfy the exact algebraic relations as at q = 10^{60}. The transfer matrices still multiply. The destructive interference isolating the q-AND remains exact. Computations executed by pebbles or photons inhabit the same Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) at identical q.

Consistency under descent. Planck-scale combinatorics aligns tightly with local continuous physics. The rationality of P_{7,6}(q) in q^{1/2} guarantees this. The amplitude remains valid over any field where q \neq 1. The polynomial governing a 3-strand braid at the Big Bang also governs it in the laboratory. The passage from discrete to continuous physics does not break logic gates; it merely attenuates the amplitude P_{7,6} and dilates the Planck step t_P(q) = q/(q-1).

At q = q_0, one has P_{7,6}(q_0) = +0.0495 and t_P(q_0) \approx 10.11. The gate operates slowly and with small amplitude, but its operation is a direct algebraic consequence of q \neq 1.

Relation to 't Hooft's CA interpretation. The thesis that quantum mechanics emerges from a deterministic Planck-scale cellular automaton aligns structurally with this framework. Both models posit discrete combinatorics at the Planck scale as the ontological primitive. Both attribute macroscopic quantum superposition to coarse-graining. The QOU aether formally substitutes 't Hooft's information loss with algebraic coarse-graining via the Markov trace on H_n(q), rendering the emergence of quantum mechanics functorial rather than statistical.
prop:reeb-turing-completeness-classical:

conj:quantum-computational-universality:

  1. (Quadratic level.) There exists a root of unity q_k = e^{2\pi i/(k+2)} with k \geq 3 and k + 2 \leq c^2 - 1 such that P_L(q_k) \neq 0. The minimal level k grows quadratically with the crossing number: k \sim c^2. Evaluation at q_k preserves all information of the computation without reduction modulo the cyclotomic ideal.

(Level k = 4, i.e. q_k = e^{2\pi i/6}, is excluded in the source: there the image is not dense.) Every quantum circuit on n qubits with N gates can be approximated to precision \epsilon by a braid \beta with c = O(N \cdot \mathrm{polylog}(1/\epsilon)) crossings.
  3. (Descent projects quantum to classical.) The descent involution \hat{\tau} decomposes the endomorphism algebra at the root-of-unity level into
  \mathrm{End}(V^{\otimes n}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}.

The descended subalgebra \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} constitutes the classical shadow: the Toffoli computation at real q. The transient complement \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} carries the quantum parallelism: exponentially many Skein resolution paths that destructively interfere upon observation. The projection \hat{\tau} represents observation. It collapses the quantum computation to the classical computation at real q. 4. (Information content.) The information content of the computation is the crossing number c. The Skein polynomial encodes up to c^2 - 1 independent coefficients representing the full quantum state. The factored form P_L(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) compresses this to O(c) observable factors.

The flow from real q to the root of unity q_k signifies the lifting of a classical computation to its quantum completion. The parameter q leaves the real axis, traverses the complex plane, and arrives on the unit circle where \mathrm{SU}(2^n) density applies. The descent involution projects back. The round-trip

  q_{\mathrm{real}} \xrightarrow{\text{lift}} q_k = e^{2\pi i/(k+2)} \xrightarrow{\hat{\tau}} q_{\mathrm{real}}

forms the quantum computation. The lift explores the Hilbert space; the descent collapses it to the observable.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real-analytic structures and numerical evaluation at the physical parameter q_0. Categorical identities drawn here remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring, but their archimedean realization is strictly specialized.
rem:skein-turing-machine:
Remark A Turing machine is a braid; its Skein decomposition is the path integral. A Turing machine computation of N gates encodes as a braid \beta on n strands with c = 3N crossings. Closing the braid yields a link L = \hat{\beta}. The Skein polynomial P_L(q) forms the output of the computation.

The Skein decomposition is the discrete path integral. At each crossing of L, the Skein relation resolves the link into three branches:

  q L_+ - q^{-1} L_- = s L_0

where s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}. Each resolution replaces one crossing with a positive (L_+), negative (L_-), or smoothed (L_0) outcome. Iterating over all c crossings constructs a resolution tree with 3^c leaves, each representing one discrete history.

This constitutes the path integral at Planck resolution. Each resolution is exactly one Planck step. Each tree path is one discrete history. The Skein polynomial sums over all 3^c histories, weighted by their crossing signs, yielding the partition function of the computation.

Path integral Skein decomposition
History Resolution path through the tree
Action weight e^{iS/\hbar} Skein weight q^{\pm 1} or s per crossing
Partition function Z Skein polynomial P_L(q) = \sum_{\text{paths}}(\text{weights})
Path integral measure Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M
Planck time step One crossing resolution

Information before and after the trace. Before the Markov trace, the braid word \beta \in H_n(q) retains the full gate address fine structure: O(N \log n) bits of exact generator wiring.

After the trace, the Skein polynomial P_L(q) compresses from 3^c paths to O(c) factors via P_L(q) = \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i(q). This is the selective erasure of internal wiring. The discrete history the universe followed is irreversibly lost. What survives is the topological invariant: the computation's output. The Markov trace acts as observation, collapsing 3^c quantum paths into one polynomial.

The backward flow. Starting from the output state E \in \Gamma(M, \mathcal{S}), one resolves each crossing backward through the jet tower. After 3N resolutions, one unwinds completely to the Big Bang initial conditions \mathcal{S}_0. By descent, all branches flow back to \mathcal{S}_0. The initial conditions are the program; the braid is the computation; the Skein polynomial is the output.

Quantum computations. A section E that factors through a finite braid word is computable: it is reachable from \mathcal{S}_0 by a finite sequence of Toffoli gates. These sections form the computable fragment of the QOU. Sections requiring infinite crossing number are non-computable. They correspond to states of the universe unattainable from the Big Bang by any finite logic sequence. This distinction represents a topological property encoded by the finite degree of the Skein polynomial.

sec:p-vs-np-boundary-intro:
What this section says about P versus NP, and what it does not. This section does not prove \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}, and nothing in it is evidence for either answer. It does three things. It translates the question into the language of skein resolution trees and horizons. It proves a number of exact algebraic facts that the translation rests on. And it locates where each QOU formulation meets the open problem. Throughout, \mathrm{P} and \mathrm{NP} are the standard classes for deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines [cook1971]. Mathlib does not define them, so no formal statement in this section is about them: wherever the formalisation names \mathrm{P} or \mathrm{NP}, they are opaque propositions, and the formal content is propositional logic about those propositions.

The translation. A computation of N gates is encoded as a braid \beta with c = 3N crossings (Skein Turing machine). Its output is the Markov trace of \beta, a Jones-type invariant of the closure L = \hat{\beta}. Expanding every crossing by the skein relation gives a resolution tree with 3^c leaves. The computational horizon is the part of that tree whose degree-0 value cannot be reached within a polynomial budget. The boundary conjecture restates \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} as non-emptiness of that horizon, and the QOU conjecture restates it as non-vanishing of an obstruction residue. Both are offered as a dictionary. Neither is a reduction, because no statement here shows that either side implies the other.

Status, sorted.

  1. Proved, with statements that can be read against Mathlib and QOU definitions. Each of these is a theorem of algebra or arithmetic. None is a theorem about \mathrm{P} or \mathrm{NP}.

    • Every trace vanishes on commutators. Hence every inner derivation a \mapsto xa - ax is invisible to every trace, and a derivation with a nonzero class in HH^1 = \mathrm{Der}/\mathrm{Inn} is not inner.
    • The Goldman–Iwahori map \theta(\sigma_i) = -\sigma_i^{-1} is an involutive automorphism of H_n(R, q) for every commutative ring R and unit q. For n \geq 2 and q + q^{-1} \neq 0 it is not inner, and it preserves the convention-D Markov trace only if q^4 = -1.
    • On a graph with edge variables in a group, a gauge change conjugates the holonomy of every closed walk, so every class function of that holonomy is unchanged. A flux change by an integer cochain \omega and a central element z multiplies the holonomy by z^{\oint \omega}, and a flux by a coboundary is a gauge change.
    • H_n(q) is semisimple at n = 2, 3, 4. For Q > 1 and X \leq 0 every Schur element is nonzero at every rank. Every real q > 1 satisfies q^k \neq 1 for every k \geq 2.
    • 2^n eventually exceeds every polynomial, and 2^n \leq 3^{3n}, so any step count s(n) with B \cdot s(n) \geq 3^{3n} is super-polynomial. This is the whole content of the physical-intractability statement in the QOU conjecture: a device that must read all 3^{3n} leaves is slow. It does not show that a device must read them.
    • A word of c matrices of size d has its trace computed with d \cdot c \cdot d^2 multiplications, which is linear in c for fixed d (bounded width). So every family of braids on a bounded number of strands has an empty computational horizon, and any family that could witness the boundary conjecture needs unboundedly many strands. By the same count, unless \mathrm{FP} = \#\mathrm{P}, the hard families of [jaeger1990] have unbounded braid index.
    • Every derivation kills every central idempotent, so it maps each Wedderburn block into itself. Automorphisms permute central idempotents, and inner automorphisms fix them (block rigidity).
    • The six tractable points of [jaeger1990] have orders 1, 2, 4, 4, 3, 3, and none has order 6 (tractable orders).

  2. Provable now, by ordinary mathematics, and not yet formalised.

    • No Hochschild room at a semisimple point. Where H_n(K, q) is split semisimple it is separable, so HH^i(H_n, M) = 0 for every i \geq 1 and every bimodule M. Every derivation is then inner, and every automorphism is inner up to a permutation of Wedderburn blocks of equal size (Skolem–Noether). The outer automorphism group at such a point is finite, and \theta acts on it as the transpose \lambda \mapsto \lambda' of partitions.
    • Semisimplicity at every rank, by formalising the criterion of [geckpfeiffer2000] on top of the Schur elements already computed.

  3. Open, tractable with new machinery, and not P versus NP.

    • Cellular automata modulo the inner ones. For quantum cellular automata, finite-depth local circuits play the role of inner automorphisms, and the index of Gross, Nesme, Vogts and Werner is an invariant of the outer class: a circuit has index 1 and a shift does not. Where Temperley–Lieb is a unitary fusion category, at suitable roots of unity, the index of the strand shift is defined, and computing it for the q-Game of Life is a tractable problem. At a non-torsion q the fusion hypothesis fails, and even the definition is open.
    • A correct non-CA theorem for intents. The proved flux-versus-gauge statement does not use locality, since a one-edge flux already changes a holonomy. The intended theorem needs the class of cellular automata restricted to curvature-preserving local gates.
    • Lower bounds in restricted models, such as the skein-expansion algorithm itself, or read-once and bandwidth-limited models with a stated access rule. Once the model is fixed these are genuine theorems. They do not reach general Turing machines.

  4. Out of reach. \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} itself, and with it every step that turns hardness of counting into hardness of deciding. Exact evaluation of the Jones polynomial is \#\mathrm{P}-hard [jaeger1990], but \#\mathrm{P}-hardness does not separate decision classes: counting perfect matchings is \#\mathrm{P}-hard, while deciding whether one exists is in \mathrm{P}. An argument that worked uniformly at every non-torsion q would also have to pass the relativization [bakergillsolovay1975], natural-proofs [razborovrudich1997] and algebrization [aaronsonwigderson2009] barriers. These steps are carried as named hypotheses with no instance, and are never discharged.

Where earlier statements say more than they prove. Read against their intent, five statements in this section go beyond their formal content.

  • "The inequality localizes strictly at the non-torsion aether." Not supported. Exact evaluation is \#\mathrm{P}-hard at every q outside a finite set, and that set excludes most roots of unity, so hardness does not single out non-torsion points. At a non-torsion point H_n(q) is semisimple, so by item 2 it has no outer derivations, and a residue described by outer derivations can only live at roots of unity.
  • "The Kummer reduction vanishes exactly at the tractable set, n \mid 6." The tractable values of V_L(t) in [jaeger1990] have orders 1, 2, 3, 4, and for t = q^{\pm 2} the orders of q are \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8\} (tractable orders). In neither convention is the set \{n : n \mid 6\}, so the claimed exact match does not hold.
  • "The residue is non-vanishing." Formally this is the fact -6 \neq 0 about a defined constant. Its reading is "-6 \neq 0", not "\chi(A) \neq 0". The value -6 comes from a separate chain with its own hypotheses.
  • "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} in the QOU." Formally this says that a given cost function \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} is not polynomially bounded. No machine model is attached to the cost function, so the statement is a schema whose meaning depends on which cost function is supplied.
  • "\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP} if and only if every horizon is empty." \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} is a statement about uniform algorithms on infinitely many inputs. The horizon is defined for one link at a time, with one fixed exponent d and one evaluation procedure, the Markov trace on the skein tree. A non-empty horizon shows that this one procedure is slow on that family. It says nothing about other algorithms.

Inner and outer automorphisms: why a fixed algebra cannot carry complexity. An observer reads traces, and a trace is blind to every inner automorphism and every inner derivation. At a semisimple point the algebra has no other continuous freedom: outer derivations vanish, and outer automorphisms form a finite group of block permutations. So at a fixed rank the algebra the observer reads is rigid, and every algebraic invariant of it, including any residue, is decided by the parameter alone. The corpus proves the matching statement for residues: a nonzero polynomial obstruction vanishes at only finitely many parameter values, so its non-vanishing is the generic case. Complexity is not a quantity of this kind. It describes how cost grows along the tower n \to \infty, for algorithms that are uniform in n, and no invariant of a single H_n(q) can encode it.

Intent and cellular automata: what an observation returns decides the question. The q-Game of Life and the Reeb flow make the QOU computationally universal, so whatever counts as polynomial time in the QOU contains ordinary \mathrm{P}, provided the simulation overhead is polynomial. The upper end depends on what one observation returns, and the corpus has not fixed this. Intent charges a cost for each inserted crossing, so reading the trace of a c-crossing braid costs on the order of c intents. If an observation returned the exact degree-0 value at that price, the QOU would evaluate the Jones polynomial exactly in polynomial time, and so solve every \#\mathrm{P} problem and every \mathrm{NP} problem. In that model "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} in the QOU" is false. If instead an observation returns a sample, as under the Born rule, the QOU behaves like a quantum computer, and the question becomes one about quantum polynomial time and \mathrm{NP}, which is at least as open as the classical one. In both cases the QOU does not supply a separation. It supplies a choice of cost model, and that choice has to be stated before any separation can be.

The blocks that follow are to be read this way: the definitions are exact, the correspondence with horizons is an analogy, and each conjecture has the status given above. The open problems are collected in the closing remark.
def:computational-horizon:
Definition Computational horizon. Let L = \hat{\beta} be the braid closure of a computation \beta with c = 3N crossings encoding N Toffoli gates, let \mathcal{R}(L) be its Skein resolution tree, with 3^c leaves, and let P_L(q) be the degree-0 observable to which the Markov trace collapses \mathcal{R}(L). A computational horizon for L is a jet horizon \mathcal{H}_c \subset \mathcal{R}(L) with the following three properties.

  1. Degree-0 opacity. The evaluation P_L(q_0), which gives the yes/no answer of the decision problem, cannot be extracted from any polynomial-depth subtree of \mathcal{R}(L).
  2. Degree \geq 1 leakage. Each individual resolution path, as degree-1 linear transport data, admits verification in O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) Planck steps by checking crossing consistencies.
  3. Bandwidth saturation. With information bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) per Planck time, extracting the degree-0 answer by exploring all 3^c paths demands
  t  \geq  \frac{c \cdot \log 3}{\mathfrak{B}(q)} \cdot  3^{c - c_0}

Planck steps whenever interference fails to bound the effective tree size polynomially.
rem:computational-horizon-remark:
Remark The computational horizon as a jet horizon on the resolution tree. A computational horizon is a barrier where evaluation outpaces verification. The resolution tree \mathcal{R}(L) of a computation has leaves representing discrete histories, and its individual resolution paths furnish witnesses.

The computational horizon applies the jet horizon directly to the resolution tree. It separates the degree-0 answer from the degree \geq 1 witnesses via a codimension-1 barrier. This barrier turns opaque when the Markov trace fails to factor the Skein polynomial into O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) terms.

Structural parallel with the jet horizon.

Jet horizon Computational horizon
Degree-0 sections vanish on \mathcal{H} The answer P_L(q_0) is inaccessible in poly time
Degree \geq 1 data leaks through Witnesses (resolution paths) are poly-time verifiable
Hawking radiation: thermal, no particle identity Partial computation: statistical correlations, no answer
Aeon boundary: separates observable epochs Complexity class boundary: separates P from NP
prop:p-bandwidth-bound:
Proposition Polynomial computation as sub-horizon bandwidth. A decision problem encoded by a link L = \hat{\beta} with c = 3N crossings belongs to \mathrm{P} if and only if its Skein polynomial P_L(q) can be evaluated (its degree-0 answer extracted) within

  t(c) \leq \mathfrak{B}(q)^{-1} \mathrm{poly}(c)

Planck steps, where \mathfrak{B}(q) = q\eta_q / (q-1)^2 is the information bandwidth per Planck time.
prf:p-bandwidth-bound:
Proof Proof of p bandwidth bound. Sketch. For the forward direction, one uses the standard simulation. If a polynomial-time Turing machine decides the problem, one encodes it as a braid with c = O(\mathrm{poly}(N)) crossings. The transfer matrix product (transfer matrix) computes P_L(q) using O(c) matrix multiplications. Each multiplication costs O(1) Planck steps.

For the converse, one observes that extracting P_L(q_0) requires resolving the value of a degree \leq c^2 - 1 polynomial at a specific point. Suppose the factored form P_L(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) has O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors. Then one computes each factor in O(1) steps from the local transfer matrix, making the total cost polynomial. If the factored form requires \omega(\mathrm{poly}(c)) factors, the Skein polynomial fails to compress. The information content of the computation exceeds the polynomial bandwidth budget.
rem:p-bandwidth-interpretation:
Remark P-class as a sub-horizon information funnel. The class \mathrm{P} consists of computations whose resolution trees exhibit sufficient destructive interference. Cancellation among the 3^c Skein histories allows the Markov trace to compress the tree to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) surviving terms. In each Planck step, the q-connection \nabla_q processes n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q iterations. Each iteration generates \eta_q q-bits of entropy. After t Planck steps, the total information budget is:

  I(t) = t \mathfrak{B}(q) = t \frac{q\eta_q}{(q-1)^2} \quad q\text{-bits.}

A \mathrm{P}-class computation succeeds when I(\mathrm{poly}(c)) suffices to determine P_L(q_0). Although the full resolution tree carries c \log_2 3 q-bits of raw information, destructive interference limits the effective content to O(\mathrm{poly}(c)) q-bits, fitting within the polynomial budget.

Three regimes.

Regime Condition Interpretation
Sub-horizon (P) Effective tree \leq \mathrm{poly}(c) Interference collapses tree; no computational horizon
Critical Effective tree = c^{O(\log c)} Quasi-polynomial; horizon marginally transparent
Super-horizon (NP-hard) Effective tree = 2^{\Omega(c)} Horizon opaque; bandwidth saturated exponentially

In the sub-horizon regime, the Markov trace funnels the 3^c paths through the degree-0 bottleneck in polynomial time. The computation avoids any computational horizon; the answer remains accessible from a polynomial-depth subtree.

In the super-horizon regime, the resolution tree retains irreducible exponential weight. The uncancelled paths carry independent information requiring full aggregation. Because the bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) per Planck step is finite, this demands exponentially many steps. A computational horizon strictly separates the answer from the observer.
def:polynomial-observable-subcategory:
Definition Polynomial observable subcategory of a resolution tree. Let \beta be a braid on n strands with c crossings, let L = \hat{\beta} be its closure, let \mathcal{R}(L) be the Skein resolution tree (Skein Turing machine), and fix a polynomial bound p(c) = c^d. For x \in \mathcal{R}(L), let \Gamma_{\mathrm{poly}}(x, A_0) be the set of degree-0 sections at x that the Markov trace computes in at most p(c) Planck steps. The polynomial observable subcategory of the resolution tree is the full sub-poset

  \mathcal{R}^{\circ}(L, q)
  = 
  \bigl\{
    x \in \mathcal{R}(L)
     : 
    \Gamma_{\mathrm{poly}}\!(x, A_0) \neq 0
  \bigr\}.

def:computational-boundary:
Definition Computational boundary of a resolution tree. Let \mathcal{R}^{\circ}(L, q) be the polynomial observable subcategory of the resolution tree. The computational boundary is the frontier

  \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = \overline{\mathcal{R}^{\circ}} \setminus \mathcal{R}^{\circ}.
rem:computational-boundary-remark:
Remark The computational boundary as a vanishing locus. Equivalently, the computational boundary is the vanishing locus of the computational horizon ideal:

  \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = V\!\bigl(\mathfrak{h}_c\bigr), \qquad
  \mathfrak{h}_c = \bigl\{ s \in \Gamma\bigl(\mathcal{R}, A_0^{\mathrm{comp}}\bigr) : s\big|_{\mathcal{H}_c} = 0 \bigr\}.

This frontier is the locus in the resolution tree where every polynomial-time degree-0 section vanishes. It structurally mirrors the jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}), substituting the resolution tower for the brane tower and the Iwahori--Hecke algebra for the Frobenius algebra.
prop:block-rigidity:
Proposition Derivations and automorphisms respect the blocks. Let A be an associative algebra over a commutative ring R, and let z \in A be a central idempotent: z^2 = z and za = az for every a \in A.

  1. Every derivation D of A satisfies D(z) = 0, and hence D(za) = z\,D(a) for every a. So D maps the block zA into itself.
  2. Every algebra automorphism of A sends central idempotents to central idempotents.
  3. Every inner automorphism x \mapsto u x u^{-1} fixes every central element. Hence an automorphism that moves a central element is not inner.

For a split semisimple Hecke algebra H_n(K, q), the central primitive idempotents are the units of the Wedderburn blocks. So no derivation mixes blocks, and an automorphism can be visibly outer at the level of the centre only by permuting blocks. The Goldman–Iwahori involution \theta(\sigma_i) = -\sigma_i^{-1} is of this kind: it exchanges the two one-dimensional characters \sigma_i \mapsto q and \sigma_i \mapsto -q^{-1}.
prf:block-rigidity:
Proof Proof that derivations and automorphisms respect the blocks. Apply the Leibniz rule to z = z^2: D(z) = D(z)z + zD(z) = 2zD(z), using that z commutes with D(z). Multiplying on the left by z gives zD(z) = 2z^2D(z) = 2zD(z), so zD(z) = 0, and then D(z) = 2zD(z) = 0. For any a, D(za) = D(z)a + zD(a) = zD(a).

If \varphi is an automorphism, then \varphi(z)^2 = \varphi(z^2) = \varphi(z), and every element of A is \varphi(b) for some b, with \varphi(z)\varphi(b) = \varphi(zb) = \varphi(bz) = \varphi(b)\varphi(z).

If z is central and u is a unit, then uzu^{-1} = zuu^{-1} = z. An automorphism of the form x \mapsto uxu^{-1} therefore fixes z, so one that moves z is not of that form. \square
conj:p-vs-np-boundary:
Conjecture \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} as jet horizon opacity. Let L = \hat{\beta} be the closure of a braid \beta encoding a decision problem. Let \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) denote its computational boundary.

  \mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP} \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) = \varnothing \text{ for every NP link } L

Consequently, \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} if and only if there exists an NP-complete link L carrying a non-empty computational horizon:

  \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} \Longleftrightarrow \exists L \text{ (NP-complete)} \text{ with } \mathcal{H}_c(L, q) \neq \varnothing.

The formal conjecture. For the QOU at a non-torsion aether parameter q_0 \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(\mathbb{R}), there exists a family of braids \{L_N = \hat{\beta}_N\}_{N \geq 1} with c_N = 3N crossings encoding an NP-complete problem such that:

  \mathcal{H}_c(L_N, q_0) \neq \varnothing \qquad \text{for all } N \geq N_0.

This non-empty boundary establishes a genuine event horizon within the resolution tree, implying \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} over \mathbb{R} at q = q_0.

prop:bounded-width-trace-cost:
Proposition A fixed-width trace costs linear time, not 3^c. Let K be a commutative semiring and let M_1, \dots, M_c be d \times d matrices over K. Applying the word to each standard basis vector, right to left, and summing the diagonal entries computes \mathrm{tr}(M_1 \cdots M_c) with d \cdot c \cdot d^2 multiplications in K. For fixed d this count is at most d^3 c, so it is not super-polynomial in c.

Consequently a braid word on a fixed number n of strands, acting through a representation of fixed dimension (the regular representation of H_n has dimension n!), has a Markov trace computable with O(c) ring operations, with no use of the 3^c leaves of the skein resolution tree. Every family of braids with bounded strand number therefore has an empty computational horizon, and any family witnessing the boundary conjecture must have unboundedly many strands. The count is in ring operations; the growth of coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], which is polynomial in c, is not counted here.
prf:bounded-width-trace-cost: Proof Proof that a fixed-width trace costs linear time. By induction on the word, applying M_1, \dots, M_c to a vector v one at a time returns (M_1 \cdots M_c)v and uses c matrix–vector products of d^2 multiplications each. Applied to the standard basis vector e_i, the i-th entry of the result is the diagonal entry (M_1 \cdots M_c)_{ii}, so summing over the d basis vectors gives the trace with d \cdot c \cdot d^2 multiplications. Since d \cdot c \cdot d^2 = d^3 \cdot c^1, the polynomial d^3 c is never exceeded. \square
rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon:
Remark P versus NP through the event horizon: information loss and computational irreversibility. One formally establishes a structural identity between computational complexity and jet horizon information loss. Reformulating \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} as the boundary condition \mathcal{H}_c \stackrel{?}{=} \varnothing equates the computational boundary with a jet horizon. The identical horizon geometry \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) that blocks degree-0 photon data between aeons simultaneously blocks the degree-0 answer of an NP-complete problem.

The dictionary. The physical QOU observer corresponds to an element of the observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)). Here, the degree-0 algebra A_0 is non-trivial and the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate. The complement (A_0 = 0) defines the jet horizon. The computational analog maps directly onto this geometry. See Table 1.

The observer in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} versus the observer in \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. In the physical QOU, observation requires \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \neq 0. The observer performs degree-0 measurements because the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate on A_0. At the jet horizon, A_0 = 0. The observer loses all degree-0 capability. It still detects degree \geq 1 data, capturing thermal winding and curvature as Hawking radiation, but it cannot identify individual particles.

In the computational setting, the observer is a polynomial-time algorithm inhabiting \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. It accesses degree-0 sections, evaluating P_L(q), strictly from nodes within \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. At the computational boundary \mathcal{H}_c, the algorithm loses degree-0 capability. It retains the ability to verify witnesses via degree-1 linear transport and detect structural correlations via degree-2 curvature data, but it cannot extract the answer. A physics-side precedent links horizons and computational hardness directly: Harlow and Hayden argue that the quantum computation needed to decode the relevant degrees of freedom from Hawking radiation takes time exponential in the entropy of the black hole, and relate the decoding task to error correction and to zero-knowledge proofs [arxiv-1301.4504v4, §3, §4.4].

Information flow across the boundary. The jet horizon leakage table applies directly to computation. See Table 2.

The degree-1 leakage embodies NP verification. Traversing a resolution path in O(c) Planck steps constitutes linear transport. It represents the first jet beyond the constant term. This checks consistency but reveals nothing concerning the global sum P_L(q_0). The degree-2 leakage embodies heuristic computation. Pairwise correlations between resolution paths reveal structural properties like clause-variable correlations. Heuristic algorithms exploit this curvature leakage without worst-case guarantees.

The Planck step as the tick of a Turing machine. Each application of the q-connection \nabla_q constitutes one Planck step. In the computational setting, this mirrors one discrete clock tick of a Turing machine. The Planck time t_P(q) = q/(q-1) sets the fundamental clock rate. The operational entropy \eta_q sets the information generated per tick.

A polynomial-time computation generates I = \mathrm{poly}(c) \cdot \eta_q / \hbar_q q-bits. For P-class problems, this suffices. Destructive interference collapses the effective resolution tree to polynomial size. For NP-complete problems, the effective tree retains exponential size. The computation generates polynomial q-bits but demands exponential q-bits of aggregated information. The bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) cannot bridge this deficit in polynomial time.

Boundary condition versus resource bound. Standard complexity theory evaluates \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} as a resource bound. The QOU translates this to a geometric statement: the interior \mathcal{R}^{\circ} is either closed (P = NP) or carries a non-trivial frontier \mathcal{H}_c (P \neq NP).

This matches the physical jet horizon. If \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} is closed, no jet horizons exist. The universe operates as a single transparent aeon without information loss. If \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} is not closed, genuine frontiers exist. The physical QOU structurally possesses jet horizons. The conjecture asserts the computational QOU similarly possesses horizons, with \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing for NP-complete braids.

The arrow of computational time. The Big Bang state initiates with A_0|_{\mathcal{S}_0} = 0. The universe begins outside \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}, behind its own jet horizon. As Planck steps accumulate, the jet tower builds degree-0 sections, moving the universe into \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}.

Computation mirrors this geometric arrow. A Turing machine begins with degree \geq 1 input data. It terminates with degree-0 output data. The computation traverses from \mathcal{R} \setminus \mathcal{R}^{\circ} into \mathcal{R}^{\circ}. For P-class problems, \mathcal{H}_c = \varnothing. The algorithm starts in \mathcal{R}^{\circ} and never leaves. For NP-complete problems, \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing. The algorithm must forcefully cross the boundary, paying the exponential depth of the resolution tree as the crossing cost. The \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} question becomes geometric: whether the computational observable subcategory covers the full resolution tree.

Conjecture \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} at non-torsion q \in \mathbb{G}_m. Conjecture (\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} in the QOU). Given a QOU with physical non-torsion aether parameter q_0 \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(\mathbb{R}), \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} holds in that QOU. This is a conditional statement: the QOU axioms are its hypothesis — it is not a claim about \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} in the abstract, and no result here would prove the unconditional Clay problem. Equivalently, the resolution-tree evaluation of the universal obstruction class \chi(A) is non-vanishing:

  \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}\!\bigl(\chi(A)\bigr)  \neq  0 \qquad\text{at } q = q_0.

The conditioning is explicit: the QOU-scoped separation is derived from the QOU faithfulness hypothesis, and a bare \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} is never concluded.

Established complexity landscape (chippable kernel). The concrete computational object attached to a link L = \hat{\beta} is its Jones invariant J_L(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)), and its complexity is a theorem, stratified by the arithmetic of q:

  • Exact evaluation is \#\mathrm{P}-hard at all but finitely many q (Jaeger--Vertigan--Welsh). The only classically poly-time points are the roots of unity of order n \mid 6 — the values q \in \{1, -1, \pm i, e^{\pm i\pi/3}\}.
  • Additive approximation is \mathrm{BQP}-complete at a primitive root of unity of order n \nmid 6 (Aharonov--Jones--Landau; Freedman--Kitaev--Larsen--Wang).

This stratification is cited fact, not a QOU derivation. Crucially, \#\mathrm{P}-hardness of one invariant's exact evaluation does not separate \mathrm{P} from \mathrm{NP}: it concerns counting, not decision, and no known reduction turns it into a \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} proof.

The \mathbb{G}_m-torsion stratification. Matching the citations above:

Regime Value of q Jones complexity
Classically transparent torsion, order n \mid 6 poly-time (JVW tractable set)
Quantum-hard torsion, order n \nmid 6 \mathrm{BQP}-complete additive approximation (AJL)
Counting-hard non-torsion q_0 \#\mathrm{P}-hard exact evaluation (JVW)

At a torsion root of unity of order n \mid 6 the Iwahori--Hecke algebra degenerates just enough that the invariant collapses to a poly-time formula. This — not torsion in general — is the transparent regime. At other roots of unity the algebra supports the AJL quantum algorithm (\mathrm{BQP}). At the non-torsion aether value q_0 the algebra is semisimple and exact evaluation is \#\mathrm{P}-hard.

Kummer persistence. The Kummer filtration yields \kappa_c^{\mathrm{comp}} \bmod n = 0 if and only if n \mid 6 — precisely the JVW classically-tractable set. Because q_0 is strictly non-torsion, no finite Kummer level applies: q_0 sits permanently outside the transparent set.

What is conjectural (the irreducible gap). The step from the established "\#\mathrm{P}-hard exact Jones evaluation at q_0" to the asserted "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}" is an analogy, not a theorem. Two things are unproven; together they constitute the QOU faithfulness hypothesis, which is open and enters only as a hypothesis, never as an established fact:

  1. that the resolution-tree residue \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}(\chi(A)) is a faithful invariant of the \mathrm{P}-vs-\mathrm{NP} decision boundary, rather than of the (easier-to-obstruct) counting problem; and
  2. that its non-vanishing at q_0 is equivalent to \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} rather than merely implied by it.

A concrete non-vanishing of \chi(A) at generic q_0 is a Zariski-open (hence generically true, easy) condition; it therefore cannot by itself discharge the conjecture without collapsing the claimed equivalence. This genericity is itself proved: a nonzero polynomial obstruction vanishes at only finitely many parameter values, so its non-vanishing locus over an infinite domain is cofinite, hence infinite — stated over a generic integral domain, with no archimedean input. This is the chippable boundary: everything above the line is cited or provable; only the analogy remains open.

The non-vanishing leg is conditional on the Wigner axiom and the branch-point count. While the observability axiom annihilates HH^0, one-dimensionality of the degree-2 obstruction space does not follow unconditionally from untwisted Hochschild Poincaré duality HH^2 \cong (HH^1)^\vee: as recorded in the Wigner axiom, for the quantum-group Hopf algebras in play the duality that holds at q \neq 1 is Brown and Zhang's Nakayama-twisted isomorphism HH^i(H, M) \cong HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M) into twisted Hochschild homology, whereas at the classical point q = 1 Whitehead's lemmas give H^1(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^2(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0. One-dimensionality \dim_k HH^2 = 1 at q \neq 1 and its archimedean evaluation onto e(TM_0) therefore enter as the explicit hypotheses (W1)--(W2) of the Wigner axiom (obstruction reduction). The remaining geometric input, the Riemann--Roch / branch-point chain that evaluates \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 (the \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 chain), reads its branch-point count off Bring's surface rather than forcing it from the categorical axioms alone. Conditional on those inputs and with q_0 strictly non-torsion, the Kummer filtration yields \mathrm{res}_{\mathcal{R}}(\chi(A)) \neq 0 at q_0 — and no step of that chain refers to computational complexity. This sharpens the collapse observation above: even conditional on the Wigner axiom, asserting the residue equivalence would derive \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} with no complexity-theoretic input, so the conjecture's complexity-theoretic burden lives entirely in items 1--2 (faithfulness of the residue for the decision boundary).

Chipping the equivalence. The conjectured equivalence decomposes into two directions, soundness \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} \Rightarrow \mathrm{res} \neq 0 and faithfulness \mathrm{res} \neq 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}, taken as separate hypotheses, from which the equivalence is derived. Given the derived non-vanishing, three facts are proved: soundness is automatic and carries no computational content; asserting the equivalence is exactly asserting \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}; and the Kummer reduction of the derived value vanishes exactly at the Jaeger--Vertigan--Welsh tractable levels, -6 \bmod n = 0 \iff n \mid 6, with any real q > 1 non-torsion. The single irreducible open item is the faithfulness direction; \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} itself enters only as an opaque proposition; no complexity-theoretic model of \mathrm{P} and \mathrm{NP} is developed here.

The counting–decision gap (companion statement). Every citable hardness result at q_0 concerns counting: Jaeger--Vertigan--Welsh give \#\mathrm{P}-hardness of exact evaluation, and \mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}} makes \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P} a consequence of \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} — the weaker separation. These enter as cited hypotheses, never as established facts. Modulo those hypotheses and the residue--semisimplicity bridge, the reachable companion faithfulness is proved: if \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P}, a surviving residue forces exact Jones evaluation at q_0 out of \mathrm{FP}. Upgrading this to the conjectured \mathrm{res} \neq 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} requires exactly two open inputs, carried as explicit hypotheses: the counting separation \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P} itself, and a counting\todecision transfer that no known result supplies. Discharging those two hypotheses is precisely what a proof of this conjecture must add. The bridge — semisimplicity of H_n(q_0) via Wenzl's root-of-unity criterion — is the one front where ordinary (non-millennium) mathematics can still advance the conjecture, and its parameter side is done: the genericity condition "q^k \neq 1 for 2 \leq k \leq n", stated over a generic monoid, is proved for every real q > 1 at every rank, and the argument composes end-to-end — for the aether q_0 > 1, given \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P}, exact Jones evaluation is not polynomial-time, conditional only on the two cited hypotheses. Notably the obstruction residual drops out of this reachable statement entirely: the counting hardness at q_0 rests on parameter genericity alone. Stage 2 advances this on the Schur-element side: semisimplicity is governed by non-vanishing of the Schur elements of the symmetrizing trace, and it is proved — on the concrete Schur element s_{\lambda,X}(Q) = Q^{n(\lambda)} \prod_x (1 - X Q^{c(x)})/(1 - Q^{h(x)}) — that in the regime Q > 1, X \leq 0 every Schur element is nonzero (positive hook lengths make every denominator strictly negative; nonpositive X makes every numerator positive). The Geck--Pfeiffer criterion enters as a cited hypothesis, and semisimplicity follows at every rank with the Schur leg computed rather than assumed. For physical Markov specialisations X = Q^{-N} > 0 the numerator factors genuinely vanish at cells of content N — the Temperley--Lieb quotient stratification. That is no longer a follow-on: it is proved, and the surviving blocks are characterised combinatorially — at X = Q^{-N} with N \geq 1 the Wedderburn blocks that survive are exactly the partitions with at most N columns, \lambda_1 \leq N.

It does not advance the open pair, and should not be cited as if it did. The aether provably never lands on the Temperley--Lieb locus: X \leq 0 \Rightarrow X \neq Q^{-N} is proved for every N, so the stratification describes a region of parameter space the aether avoids. The reachable counting statement consumes only semisimplicity at q_0, already discharged by Wenzl genericity from q_0 > 1; knowing which blocks die elsewhere is not one of its inputs, and fewer surviving blocks would mean a smaller algebra — the tractable direction, not the hard one. Nor is it a counting-versus-decision statement, so it cannot supply the transfer. What remains open beyond all citation is unchanged: the pair of open hypotheses of the transfer statement above.

What the QOU actually proves (the derived result, not the Clay separation). Where the conjectured \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} needs the open counting\todecision transfer, a weaker but genuinely derived statement needs none of it. The observation trace at q_0 is \#\mathrm{P}-hard (above); if extracting the degree-0 answer requires the full 3^{3n}-leaf surviving resolution tree, the Bekenstein bandwidth bound forces any bandwidth-limited device to run super-polynomially — no bandwidth-limited device decides the boundary problem in polynomial time. This physical-intractability theorem is proved, as is the exponential-domination fact it rests on. It is strictly weaker than abstract \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} — a general Turing machine is not bandwidth-limited — but it is derived, not assumed.

The fourth millennium evaluation. The QOU obstruction reduction conjectures that all classical-limit obstructions map to the scalar class \chi(A) \in HH^2 \cong k, so that \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} becomes a fourth restriction of the same class alongside RH, NS, and BSD. The proportionality of the four evaluations is part of the conjecture, not a consequence of it.

Corollary (conditional). If the obstruction-class conjecture holds, resolving \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} constrains RH, NS, and BSD and vice versa, their evaluation maps differing but the underlying class remaining identical. The corollary inherits the conjectural status of its hypothesis.
prop:jvw-tractable-orders: Proposition Orders of the Jones-tractable points. Jaeger, Vertigan and Welsh show that exact evaluation of the Jones polynomial V_L(t) is \#\mathrm{P}-hard except at the six points t \in \{1, -1, i, -i, e^{2\pi i/3}, e^{-2\pi i/3}\} [jaeger1990]; this is cited, not derived. These six points are primitive roots of unity of orders 1, 2, 4, 4, 3, 3. None of them is a primitive 6th root of unity, and i has order 4, which does not divide 6. So with t = q the orders of the tractable points form the set \{1, 2, 3, 4\}, not \{n : n \mid 6\}. With t = q^{\pm 2} the orders of q form \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8\}, which is not \{n : n \mid 6\} either.
prf:jvw-tractable-orders: Proof Proof of the orders of the Jones-tractable points. 1 has order 1 and -1 has order 2. Since i^2 = -1 and i^4 = 1, i is a primitive 4th root of unity, and -i = i^3 is one too because \gcd(3, 4) = 1. The number \omega = e^{2\pi i/3} is a primitive cube root of unity, and so is \omega^{-1}. A primitive root of unity has a unique order, so none of the six points is a primitive 6th root. Finally 4 \nmid 6. \square
rem:skein-filtration-trichotomy:
Remark One length filtration, three problems: q-Collatz halting, P vs NP, q-NS regularity. Three hard problems reformulated inside a quantum observable universe — the q-Collatz halting question, the P versus NP boundary, and q-Navier–Stokes regularity — are the same question asked of one length filtration on the Skein aether \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. Each computation is a braid word \beta \in H_n(q); its observed output is the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) (the Jones–Skein invariant an observer reads); and its complexity is graded by the crossing-number filtration \ell.

Write \ell for that filtration and \mathrm{obs} for the Markov-trace observation. The three problems differ only in what they ask of \ell along an orbit:

Reformulation Question on the filtration \ell
q-Collatz does \ell descend to the normal form (the orbit halts)?
P versus NP is the observation reachable within a polynomial \ell-budget, rather than the naive 3^{c} resolution leaves?
q-Navier–Stokes does \ell stay bounded (no finite-time blow-up of the vortex-knot complexity)?

The observation is the common, tractable shadow: because the Skein relations cut a single fixed ideal whose quotient is \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], the Markov trace is computable, so "the observed output reaches the normal form's value" follows from halting for free. The difficulty is not algebraic — it does not live in an ideal. By the Reeb-flow Turing-completeness of the aether dynamics, the halting set is undecidable, hence not cut out by any ideal; the content sits entirely in the filtration \ell.

For q-Navier–Stokes the dictionary is concrete: a vortex tube of the brane fluid is a braid word evolving in time, its closure is a knotted vortex, its conserved helicity is the Markov-trace observation, and its crossing number is \ell. A non-increasing filtration — a monotone Lyapunov complexity, the categorical form of bounded enstrophy — rules out blow-up with bound the initial complexity, the abstract shadow of the q-Beale–Kato–Majda criterion.

The legs are coupled, not merely parallel. Two consequences of the shared filtration are proved. First, a counterexample on either the descent leg or the boundedness leg destroys the shared ingredient — a controlled descent on \ell — from which the two positive conclusions are jointly derived, so the walls do not fail independently. Second, within any single system whose normal form is periodic, the boundedness question and the descent question are coupled outright: an orbit whose filtration is unbounded cannot reach the normal form, because a halting orbit lands in the attractor's cycle and thereafter visits only finitely many states, hence has bounded complexity with an explicit bound depending on that orbit. The implication runs one way only — a bounded orbit may cycle forever without ever reaching the normal form — which is why descent is the harder of the two questions.

This couples two questions asked of one instance; it does not identify a Navier--Stokes singularity with a q-Collatz divergence. The two legs are instantiated here as different systems — the q-Collatz system, whose complexity measure is a free parameter, and the vortex-reduction system, on which unbounded complexity is not even satisfiable, since that system is proved regular. Sharing the abstraction \mathtt{SkeinObservationSystem} is sharing a type, not a state.

The hypothesis the coupling needs is that the normal form be periodic, and the q-Collatz attractor satisfies it: the class \mathrm{QCollatz} carries \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{C}(\alpha)) = \alpha for the attractor \alpha, the 2-cycle \{q^{-1}, 1 + q^{-1}\} that is the q-lift of the classical \{1, 2\}. The discharge is recorded as a lemma rather than asserted, since \mathcal{C}(\mathcal{C}(\alpha)) = \alpha is periodicity at period 2 definitionally. The hypothesis is periodicity rather than the more obvious fixed-point condition \mathcal{C}(\alpha) = \alpha because that condition is not merely stronger, it is false here — the same class carries \mathcal{C}(\alpha) \neq \alpha as an axiom. A transfer stated for fixed points would be vacuous on precisely the system it was written for.

A descent measure is not a cheaper target than the conjecture. Since descent implies halting, it is tempting to read "find a descent measure for \ell" as a weaker goal than "prove q-Collatz". It is not: on a forward-invariant cone the two are equivalent, because if every element halts then the hitting time \mu(P) = \min\{k : \mathcal{C}_q^k(P) = \alpha\} is itself a strict \mathbb{N}-valued descent measure. So any search whose success criterion is the mere existence of a descent measure is searching for a restatement of the conjecture.

This sharpens rather than abandons the descent route. Its point is that an explicit, independently motivated \mu — a valuation, a degree, a contact volume — can discharge the conjecture; a candidate is worth pursuing precisely for the properties the hitting time lacks, namely computability, a closed form, and monotonicity under the algebra of [2]_q and [3]_q. The obvious candidate v_{[2]} is already refuted, scope-(a): the q-odd element P = -q^{-1} - 2 has v_{[2]}(P) = 0 while its odd branch has v_{[2]} = 2 — one candidate excluded, the class untouched.

The three legs share the aether and diverge only in the filtration question; none is settled here. Each remains an open conjecture in its own right: the q-Collatz descent measure, the faithfulness leg of the P versus NP boundary, and q-Navier–Stokes regularity are the respective open cores. What the shared structure supplies is a common language in which the tractable observation and the hard filtration question are cleanly separated.
thm:geometry-of-incompleteness:
Theorem The geometry of incompleteness: a Turing-complete QOU has a nonempty horizon. Given a QOU whose aether is Turing-complete, the jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) is non-empty: there exists a degree-0 datum whose truth is inaccessible. Equivalently, the degree-0 sections vanish on a non-trivial region, \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_0) = 0.

A degree-0 datum is an observable answer read off the aether — a decision result, a particle identity, or the truth value of a self-referential sentence. It is inaccessible — behind the horizon — when it fails either route to access:

  • formally, it is unprovable (Gödel incompleteness, forced in any aether expressive enough to encode arithmetic — every q \neq 1 aether, whose q-Toffoli gates are universal); or
  • physically, extracting it is super-polynomial. For the boundary family a bandwidth-limited device must read the full 3^{3n}-leaf surviving skein resolution tree, so by the Bekenstein bandwidth bound its step count grows faster than every polynomial (the physical-intractability theorem).

These are two witnesses of one phenomenon — the vanishing of degree-0 sections. Gödel supplies a formally-inaccessible degree-0 datum; the resolution-tree information bound supplies a physically-intractable one. Either establishes a non-empty horizon; the QOU exhibits both, so the horizon is doubly confirmed. In the framework's reading, this common cause is exactly what a black-hole event horizon is: the region across which degree-0 truth cannot pass while degree-\geq 1 data (witnesses, Hawking radiation) leaks. The event horizon is the geometry of incompleteness.

Scope (what this does and does not say). This is an existence / necessity statement about the aether's structure — a Turing-complete QOU must host an inaccessible degree-0 region. It is not a proof of \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}. The step from "the observation trace is intractable to extract" to "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP}" is a counting-to-decision transfer that no known result supplies and that a generic argument cannot (a \#\mathrm{P}-hard count can sit atop a poly-time decision, as for perfect matchings). The physical-intractability leg is genuinely derived; the formal-incompleteness leg is Gödel's theorem; only the identification of this joint inaccessibility with the black-hole horizon is the framework's degree-0 interpretation.
rem:p-vs-np-open-problems:
Remark Open problems around P versus NP in the QOU. The following problems are open. They are listed with what is known and what each would and would not settle. Only the first is \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP}; the rest are ordinary mathematics that the section's statements depend on.

  1. The counting-to-decision transfer. Exact evaluation of the Jones polynomial is \#\mathrm{P}-hard [jaeger1990], and \mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}} gives \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} \Rightarrow \mathrm{FP} \neq \#\mathrm{P}. The converse direction is what every QOU formulation would need, and it is \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} itself. A uniform argument over all non-torsion q must pass the relativization [bakergillsolovay1975], natural-proofs [razborovrudich1997] and algebrization [aaronsonwigderson2009] barriers. Out of reach.

  2. What an observation returns. The cost model of the QOU is not yet fixed by the definition of observation. If an observation of a c-crossing braid returns the exact degree-0 value at a cost linear in c, as intent suggests, then QOU polynomial time contains \#\mathrm{P} and hence \mathrm{NP}, and "\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} in the QOU" is false. If it returns a sample, the question is one about quantum polynomial time. Choosing between these is a definition, not a theorem, and it has to be made before any QOU-scoped separation can be stated.

  3. Polynomial overhead of universality. The q-Game of Life is universal for reversible computation, and the Reeb flow simulates Turing machines. For "QOU polynomial time contains \mathrm{P}" one needs the simulation of a Turing machine to have polynomial overhead in the QOU cost model of item 2. Not yet proved.

  4. Outer derivations at roots of unity. By block rigidity, no derivation mixes the blocks of a split semisimple H_n(K, q), and by separability HH^{i} = 0 for i \geq 1 there. At a root of unity H_n(\zeta) can be non-semisimple and HH^1 can be nonzero. Computing \dim HH^1(H_n(\zeta)) for small n and \zeta is finite linear algebra and tractable. It would locate where an outer residue can live. It cannot carry complexity, because it is an invariant of one algebra of fixed rank.

  5. Separability in Lean. Formalise that a split semisimple algebra over a field has HH^i(A, M) = 0 for i \geq 1, and the Skolem–Noether description of its automorphisms as inner automorphisms composed with permutations of equal-size blocks. Formalise semisimplicity of H_n(q) at every rank via [geckpfeiffer2000] on top of the computed Schur elements. Standard and tractable.

  6. Trace-preserving outer automorphisms. Classify the automorphisms of H_n(K, q) that preserve the Markov trace. By item 5 they permute blocks of equal size and equal trace weight. The Goldman–Iwahori involution preserves no Markov trace with q^4 \neq -1. Tractable.

  7. Cellular automata modulo inner ones. For quantum cellular automata, finite-depth local circuits play the role of inner automorphisms, and the index of Gross, Nesme, Vogts and Werner is an invariant of the outer class. Where Temperley–Lieb is a unitary fusion category, at suitable roots of unity, the index of the strand shift of the q-Game of Life is defined and can be computed. At a non-torsion q the fusion hypothesis fails and the index is not even defined. Tractable at roots of unity; open as a definition elsewhere.

  8. A correct non-CA theorem for intents. The gauge-versus-flux distinction for edge variables is proved and does not use locality, since a one-edge flux already changes a holonomy. The intended statement, that a flux-threading intent is not a cellular automaton, needs the automata restricted to curvature-preserving local gates. Tractable once that class is defined.

  9. Lower bounds in restricted models. The skein-expansion algorithm reads 3^c leaves, and bounded width shows other algorithms need not. Lower bounds against a fixed model, such as read-once evaluation or a bandwidth-limited device with a stated access rule, are genuine theorems once the model is fixed. They do not reach general Turing machines.
sec:q-heat-kernel-analysis-intro:
The aether supplies a Jackson derivative D_q and a categorical Fourier transform. One now constructs the corresponding heat kernel and extracts its spectral decomposition. This section verifies that standard heat-kernel analysis survives the q-deformation when q = q_0 is non-torsion. It also establishes a computational fallback when the Peter--Weyl sum diverges at large rank.

The construction proceeds in three steps. First, the Taylor series proposition realises the abstract grouplike \exp_q as a convergent power series. Second, the q-Gaussian proposition confirms that the q-Gaussian solves the fundamental q-heat equation \partial_t u = D_q^2 u. Third, the Peter--Weyl decomposition expands this solution in Hecke--Wedderburn characters. The closing remark provides a Perron--Frobenius truncation for large-rank evaluation. The subsequent section on Statistical Mechanics leverages this q-heat kernel as the partition function Z_q to derive quantum temperature, pressure, and volume.
prop:q-exponential-taylor:
Proposition Taylor series of \exp_q (archimedean). Let R be a commutative ring of characteristic zero in which all Jackson factorials [n]_q! = \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1 - q^k}{1 - q} are invertible. Over R, the convergent power series

  \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{x^n}{[n]_q!}

represents the abstract grouplike \exp_q \in G(\mathcal{H}_q).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at q_0. Categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is strictly specialised here.
prf:q-exponential-taylor:
Proof Proof of q exponential taylor. The categorical defining equation D_q\, \exp_q = \exp_q, joined with the boundary condition \exp_q(0) = 1, determines a unique formal power series \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n\ge 0} a_n x^n in R[\![x]\!]. The Jackson derivative acts on monomials via D_q(x^n) = [n]_q\, x^{n-1}. One substitutes this into the equation:

  D_q\,\sum_n a_n x^n
  \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n [n]_q x^{n-1}
  \;=\; \sum_{m \ge 0} a_{m+1} [m+1]_q x^m.

Equating this to \sum_m a_m x^m forces the recursion a_{m+1} = a_m / [m+1]_q. With a_0 = 1, one obtains:

  a_n \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{[k]_q} \;=\; \frac{1}{[n]_q!}.

This verifies the claimed coefficient. Convergence on a neighbourhood of 0 holds because [n]_q! \to \infty faster than geometrically when |q| < 1 or |q| > 1. When |q| = 1, write q = e^{2\pi i\theta}; for irrational \theta convergence holds by Diophantine estimates on \theta. This series provides the archimedean realisation of the universal grouplike. Its existence over \mathbb{C} forms a theorem about the \mathbb{C}-fibre of the moduli of grouplikes over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], not a redefinition of \exp_q. \qed

Special values.

Regime [n]_q! asymptotic \exp_q(x) behaviour
q = 1 n! (classical) \exp_q(x) = e^x (ordinary exponential)
0 < q < 1 (1 - q)^{-n}\,n!\,(1 + O(q^n)) slow-growth; radius \infty
q > 1 q^{\binom{n}{2}}\,n!_{q^{-1}} faster-than-classical growth
q \to \infty q^{\binom{n}{2}} entire, type \log q

Relation to physical constants. Evaluating at the QOU aether value q_0 (local aether q) yields e_{q_0}(x) = \sum x^n / [n]_{q_0}!. This series generates the moments of the Reeb-flow distribution on \mathcal{S}. Because [n]_{q_0}! \sim q_0^{\binom{n}{2}} n!_{q_0^{-1}} grows super-exponentially at q_0 \approx 1.11, the series converges for all x \in \mathbb{C}.
